message.content: {"caption":"Schematic of validation-gated skill editing compared with unstable ad hoc updates, with an inset analogy to text-space optimization.","description":"A conceptual 3D optimization diagram. A curved surface with contour lines rises in orange at the upper-left and descends into a blue low region at the lower-right. The vertical axis is labeled “Val. Error”; a diagonal floor axis is labeled “Skill Space,” and another diagonal floor arrow points toward the right. A document labeled “S₀” marks the starting skill on the higher-error part of the surface. A solid blue, arrowed path proceeds downhill from it through a sequence of small edit/gate symbols bearing green checks and ends at a document representing a better task-specific skill. This path is labeled “bounded skill edits” and “stable, controlled optimization.” A nearby label, “held-out selection gate,” identifies the acceptance checks. Red dashed arrows branch away from the path toward the left/downhill side and are labeled “rejected side updates.” In contrast, broad gray dashed arrows make larger, irregular jumps across the surface; the labels “ad hoc updates” and “large semantic jumps, unstable updates” describe these paths. A separate document on the blue slope is labeled “suboptimal skill.” At lower right, the better-skill document connects by branching gray lines to three rounded labels: “better task-specific ability,” “cross-model / harness generalization,” and “low-cost transfer and iteration.” An upper-right inset shows an input x directed into a neural-network schematic and an output arrow labeled y; the network is marked f and has a snowflake symbol above it, indicating a frozen model. Beside the input is a document labeled “Skill S” with a flame icon, depicting the skill artifact being optimized while the model remains fixed. Below, a panel titled “Text-space optimization analogy” maps: parameter → skill document; gradient direction → trajectory-derived edit direction; learning rate → edit budget; validation check → held-out selection gate; stable training setting → batch / minibatch / schedule / gate.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
